text:
JC 1839

SUPERIOR COURT

CANADA

PROVINCE OF QUEBEC

DISTRICT OF

MONTREAL

No:

500-12-255373-007

DATE:

MARCH 8, 2002

______________________________________________________________________

By:

THE HONOURABLE

JUSTICE LOUIS CRÊTE

______________________________________________________________________

S…  D…,

Plaintiff,

v.

DA… D…,

Defendant.

______________________________________________________________________

J U D G M E N T

______________________________________________________________________

[
1
]

WHEREAS the parties are currently involved in
divorce proceedings which have yet to be decided on the merits;

[
2
]

WHEREAS at the outset in mid-November 2000 the
parties reached a formal agreement on provisional measures, which was ratified
by a court order, dated December 5, 2000;

[
3
]

WHEREAS the parties agreed that their two
children, R... and J..., would reside primarily with Mrs D..., while Mr D...
would exercise standard access rights;

[
4
]

WHEREAS the parties agreed that Mr D... would
pay his wife S… $3,000 per month as child support for the upkeep of R... and
J... and, in addition, pay for the schooling costs associated with the private
school attended by the children, up to a maximum of $20,000 a year;

[
5
]

WHEREAS the parties agreed that Mr D... would
pay his wife spousal support in the amount of $1,384.60 a week, being
equivalent to $6,000 a month;

[
6
]

WHEREAS the amounts of child and spousal support
were predicated upon an annual income by Mr D... in excess of $550,000;

[
7
]

WHEREAS on May 8
th
, 2001 Mr D... filed
and served a Motion to modify provisional measures asking for a substantial
reduction of his alimentary obligations

vis-à-vis both his children and his wife, on the basis of an alleged important
drop in his revenues;

[
8
]

WHEREAS on May 9
th
2001 Mrs D... filed
her own Motion to modify provisional measures where by she, inter alia, asked
for an increase in spousal support from $6,000 to $14,058.26 a month;

[
9
]

WHEREAS Mrs D... also filed a Motion for
provision for costs which she later amended to now request the granting of a
provision totalling $14,500;

[
10
]

WHEREAS on May 15
th
2001 Mr Justice
Pierre Tessier issued an interim order in favour of Mr D... reducing his child
support obligation to a sum of $2,500 and his spousal support obligation to
$4,000 a month;

[
11
]

WHEREAS Mr D... later made a Motion for
permission to sell the family residence where none of the parties any longer
resided;

[
12
]

WHEREAS the parties' four Motions were heard and
argued together over a three-day period;

[
13
]

WHEREAS on the last day of hearing before the
Court the parties consented to judgment on Mr D...' Motion to sell the family
residence;

[
14
]

WHEREAS the main contentious issue between the
parties relates to the amount of child and spousal support that ought to be
paid by Mr D... for the upkeep of his children and his wife S…;

[
15
]

WHEREAS Mr D... is currently employed as a
stockbroker, but claims he now earns $350,416 a year instead of the $550,000 he
was earning at the time of the consent agreement in November 2000;

[
16
]

WHEREAS the Court has to evaluate Mr D...' revenues
in order to determine the equitable amount of support he ought to pay for the
upkeep of his children and his wife;

[
17
]

CONSIDERING that the evidence has established
that Mr D...' revenues have diminished since the consent agreement, in large
part due to the fact that he is paid on a percentage basis of the market value
of his clients' portfolios and that the technology stocks meltdown in 2001 has
significantly reduced the value of said portfolios, reducing thereby Mr D...'
own revenues;

[
18
]

CONSIDERING that at the time of the consent
agreement in November 2000 the latest income tax form then available showed for
Mr D... an employment income of $623,224 for the fiscal year of 1999 with
expenses of $68,372.50;

[
19
]

CONSIDERING that for the year 2001, after the
technology stocks meltdown,

Mr D... employment income will be in the neighbourhood of $460,000, as per Mr
F… T…'s testimony;

[
20
]

CONSIDERING that one has to deduct from said
employment income the expenses paid to generate such income;

[
21
]

CONSIDERING that the Court evaluates those
expenses to be approximately $70,000, based on past years' experience and the
figures advanced by Mr T… and Mr D...;

[
22
]

CONSIDERING that, for the purpose of setting the
amount of child and spousal support, the Court cannot take into consideration
certain liabilities alleged by Mr D... and relating namely to the legal fees he
has to pay for his sister-in-law, which fees were known to him at the time of
the consent agreement, and relating also to tax assessments which were made
against him by the revenue departments in recent months;

[
23
]

CONSIDERING that, under the terms of
section 17

of the
Divorce Act
, Mr D... has established a sufficiently important change in
his financial capacities to justify the variation of the initial support order,
given the fact that such change in his financial capacities could not be
foreseen, at least not in such magnitude;

[
24
]

CONSIDERING that under the circumstances the
Court has to assess the respective needs and means of the parties in light of
their new financial situation;

[
25
]

CONSIDERING that Mr D...' current revenues are
now $390,000 a year ($460,000 - $70,000 (expenses)) and not the $350,000 that
he claimed in his statement of income and expenditures;

[
26
]

CONSIDERING that Mrs D... has no income
whatsoever, having remained at home for the last 15 years to take care of the
couple's children;

[
27
]

CONSIDERING that Mrs D...' demand for spousal
support in the amount of $14,058.26 a month (i.e. almost $170,000 a year) is
excessive, especially in light of the fact that a sum of $6,000 spousal support
has been agreed upon by the parties at a time where Mr D...' annual revenues
were 40% higher than they are now;

[
28
]

CONSIDERING that Mrs D...' statement of income
and expenditures detailing monthly expenses of $9,372.17
net
is greatly
exaggerated;

[
29
]

CONSIDERING that conversely, the Court cannot
accept the exaggerated expense figures appearing on Mr D...' own statement of
income and expenditures, in view of the fact that such expenses show, inter
alia, a figure of $25,000
a year
for the purchases of furniture and
appliances, $2,000 in toys and gifts, $4,000 in taxis and public transport,
$3,600 children's allowance etc.;

[
30
]

CONSIDERING that the statements of either party
can therefore not be of great help to assist the Court in determining the real
needs of the parties;

[
31
]

CONSIDERING, however, that an effective
guideline can be derived from the balance struck by the parties themselves in
their consent agreement of November 2000;

[
32
]

CONSIDERING that Mrs D..., who is without
employment and without any immediately marketable training cannot be expected
to be financially autonomous overnight;

[
33
]

CONSIDERING that, on the basis of the income
currently earned by Mr D... ($390,000) and using,
mutantis mutandis,
the
Aliform he has provided the Court with, he ought to be paying $26,965 in child
support instead of the $36,000 decided upon in the consent agreement;

[
34
]

CONSIDERING, however, that under the consent
agreement Mr D... had agreed to pay for his children's private schooling costs,
up to a yearly maximum of $20,000;

[
35
]

CONSIDERING that, pursuant to a common decision
by their parents, R... and J... were inscribed in a private school that
provides them with a good education, and that it would constitute an undue
hardship in the circumstances to take them out of that school at the present
time;

[
36
]

CONSIDERING J...'s particular behaviour
difficulties which are somewhat alleviated by his going to the Priory private
school which gives him a secure schooling environment;

[
37
]

CONSIDERING that Mr D... should therefore
continue to pay for the costs related to his two children's private schooling,
to the same extent as that provided for in the consent agreement;

[
38
]

CONSIDERING that Mrs D... still needs spousal
support pending the divorce proceedings;

[
39
]

CONSIDERING the now reduced financial capacity
of Mr D... in light of the decrease in his professional income;

[
40
]

CONSIDERING that Mrs D... should not be unduly
penalized nor be condemned to live with radically reduced means of living,
given the level of expenses she had been accustomed to during the marriage;

[
41
]

CONSIDERING, however, that Mrs D... should
realize at this juncture that she cannot expect to obtain the same amount of
spousal support, not to mention the increase she is asking for, in view of her
husband's diminished financial capacity;

[
42
]

CONSIDERING that Mrs D... has shown a certain
misunderstanding of what should be a balanced family budget, in that she
appears to be spending much more that what her financial means warrant;

[
43
]

CONSIDERING that spousal support paid by Mr D...
is deductible from his income, for tax purposes;

[
44
]

CONSIDERING that some of the twenty-four
conclusions of Mrs D...' Motion are justified, namely the conclusions in
paragraphs h,) i), and r);

[
45
]

CONSIDERING that, in view of Mrs D...' complete
financial dependency, she is not able to pay her attorney, especially in the
context of a variation order that was served at the initiative of Mr D...;

[
46
]

CONSIDERING that Mrs D...' Motion for security
for costs is therefore well founded, at least in part, in view of her financial
dependency;

[
47
]

WHEREFORE THE COURT:

[
48
]

GRANTS, but in part only, Mr Da… D...' Motion to
modify provisional measures;

[
49
]

REDUCES from $3,000 to $2,250 per month the
child support Mr D... ought to provide his wife with for the upkeep of their
two minor children R... and J...;  and ORDERS therefore Mr D... to pay said
reduced monthly amount, this order being retroactive to the 1
st
of
June 2001;

[
50
]

ORDERS Mr D... to continue paying for his
children's private schooling costs, as provided in the consent agreement on
provisional measures signed by the parties on November 14 and 16, 2000;

[
51
]

ORDERS Mr D... to pay his wife S… D... spousal
support in the amount of $4,500 a month, this order being retroactive to June 1
st

2001;

[
52
]

GRANTS, but in part only, Mrs D... Motion to
modify provisional measures;

[
53
]

ORDERS Mr D... to permit Mrs D... to obtain, and
continue with, any professional medical and psychological assistance
recommended by the school and/or the Jewish General Hospital, as required by
the children R... and J...;

[
54
]

ORDERS the parties not to discuss the issues
between them with their children and ORDERS Mr D... not to harass or threaten
Mrs D... in any way;

[
55
]

ORDERS Mr D... to sign any and all documents
required to enable

Mrs D... to make the medical and dental submissions directly to the insurer;

[
56
]

GRANTS, but in part only, Mrs D... amended
Motion for provision for costs and;

[
57
]

ORDERS Mr D... to pay Mrs D... a provision for
costs in the amount of $10,000 within 60 days of this judgment;

[
58
]

THE WHOLE, each party paying its costs.

LOUIS CRÊTE, J.S.C.

Me Rajpattie Persaud

Attorney for Plaintiff

Me Katherine MacLeod

Ebrahim MacLeod &
Gervais
